title: 20th Century History Quiz: 20 Questions
description: Take our free 20th century history quiz: 20 questions on the space race, Cold War, decolonization, and more. Easy to expert, with facts after each answer.
h1: 20th Century History Quiz: From Sputnik to Soviet Collapse
intro: The 20th century brought world wars, revolutions, independence movements, the Cold War, and the first steps into space. This quiz focuses on the second half of the century, with 20 questions about the leaders, events, and turning points that shaped the modern world. The early questions are famous moments you may remember from school, the middle ones ask for key names and dates, and the final four are expert challenges. You get about five seconds per question, and every answer includes a short, factual explanation. It's free and fast. Ready to travel through the century?

questions.q: Which Soviet cosmonaut became the first person in space in 1961?
questions.explication: Gagarin completed a single orbit of Earth aboard Vostok 1 on April 12, 1961.

questions.q: Which satellite launched by the USSR in 1957 was the first artificial satellite?
questions.explication: Sputnik 1 was a metal sphere about the size of a beach ball, and its launch started the space race.

questions.q: Which crisis in October 1962 brought the world close to nuclear war?
questions.explication: The U.S. and USSR stood off over Soviet missiles in Cuba for 13 days until a deal was reached.

questions.q: Which anti-apartheid leader was freed in 1990 after 27 years in prison?
questions.explication: Mandela was released on February 11, 1990, and became South Africa's president in 1994.

questions.q: Which U.S. mission landed the first humans on the Moon in July 1969?
questions.explication: Neil Armstrong and Buzz Aldrin walked on the Moon while Michael Collins orbited above.

questions.q: Which international organization was founded in 1945 to maintain peace?
questions.explication: The UN was founded after World War II with 51 original member states.

questions.q: Which civil rights leader delivered the "I Have a Dream" speech in 1963?
questions.explication: King spoke to more than 200,000 people at the March on Washington on August 28, 1963.

questions.q: Which leader is best known for the 1930 Salt March in India?
questions.explication: Gandhi led thousands on a march of about 390 km (240 miles) to protest British salt taxes.

questions.q: Which U.S. president was assassinated in Dallas in 1963?
questions.explication: Kennedy was shot on November 22, 1963, and Lyndon Johnson was sworn in as president the same day.

questions.q: Which Soviet leader launched the reforms known as perestroika and glasnost?
questions.explication: Gorbachev's reforms of the late 1980s aimed to restructure the economy and open up public debate.

questions.q: Which 1957 treaty created the European Economic Community?
questions.explication: Six countries signed it in Rome: France, West Germany, Italy, Belgium, the Netherlands, and Luxembourg.

questions.q: In which Soviet republic was the Chernobyl nuclear plant, the site of a 1986 accident?
questions.explication: The plant is located in northern Ukraine, near the border with Belarus.

questions.q: Who proclaimed the People's Republic of China in 1949?
questions.explication: Mao announced the new state in Beijing on October 1, 1949, after the Communists won the civil war.

questions.q: Who was the first woman in space, in 1963?
questions.explication: Tereshkova orbited Earth 48 times aboard Vostok 6 in June 1963.

questions.q: In which year was the Soviet Union dissolved?
questions.explication: The USSR formally ceased to exist on December 26, 1991, giving rise to 15 independent countries.

questions.q: Which war began in June 1950 when North Korean forces crossed into South Korea?
questions.explication: An armistice in July 1953 ended the fighting, but no peace treaty was signed.

questions.q: Which 1955 conference gathered newly independent Asian and African nations in Indonesia?
questions.explication: Leaders from 29 countries discussed cooperation and opposition to colonialism, helping lay the groundwork for the Non-Aligned Movement.

questions.q: Which country experienced the Carnation Revolution in 1974?
questions.explication: A largely bloodless military coup ended decades of dictatorship and led to the independence of Portugal's African colonies.

questions.q: Which canal did Egypt's Nasser nationalize in 1956, sparking an international crisis?
questions.explication: Britain, France, and Israel responded militarily, but pressure from the U.S. and USSR forced them to withdraw.

questions.q: Which British colony, once called the Gold Coast, became independent in 1957?
questions.explication: Ghana, led by Kwame Nkrumah, was the first sub-Saharan African colony to gain independence from European rule in the postwar era.

faq: Which events does this 20th century quiz focus on?

Most questions come from the second half of the century: the space race, the Cold War, civil rights, decolonization, and the collapse of the Soviet Union. A few touch on earlier events. For the world wars, try our dedicated World War 1 and World War 2 quizzes.

The Cold War was a long period of political and military rivalry between the United States and the Soviet Union and their allies, roughly from 1947 to 1991. It was "cold" because the two superpowers never fought each other directly, but they competed through arms races, alliances, proxy wars, and the space race.
Can I use this quiz in class?

Yes. The questions are factual and cover widely taught topics, so the quiz works well as a review or warm-up. Students can read the short explanation after each answer, then replay the quiz to improve. It's free and requires no signup.
